text: A half-column that has struck in the Swift sub-step does not strike in the normal sub-step, even if the unit that gave it Swift has since left the column, and even if a new unit has since been put into that column. A half-column that has struck in the normal sub-step does not strike in the Sluggish sub-step, even if it has since gained Sluggish. A half-column that struck in the Swift sub-step and has Sluggish in the Sluggish sub-step strikes again then (rule 608.2c). This record belongs to the half-column, not to the units in it, and it stays with that column if the columns are renumbered (for example, when a new column is opened to its left).

text: In a split step, each sub-step that was scheduled, when the step began, to have a half-column strike in it is a separate step. After each such sub-step except the last scheduled one, the abilities that triggered during it are put on the stack and players receive priority; the next sub-step deals no damage until that stack has resolved and all players have passed priority in succession with it empty. State-based changes (deaths, back-row units moving forward, lost shared attributes) have already happened when this window opens.

text: Between sub-steps, the game's state is updated before anything else: units with lethal damage are destroyed, a unit behind a removed unit moves to the front row, and attributes shared by a removed unit are lost. Columns do not close gaps after blocks have been declared.

text: If combat damage that would be dealt to a player is dealt to a unit instead (as Oorblak's ability does), the replacement applies to that damage once. Without Piercing, all of that damage is dealt to the unit. With Piercing, the damage beyond the unit's lethal damage is still combat damage that would be dealt to the player: another such effect that has not applied (a second Oorblak) may take it, the same one may not, and what none takes is dealt to the player. A redirect applies before an effect that changes how combat damage is dealt to a player (Blightsea Polyp); that effect applies only to damage actually dealt to the player, such as Piercing excess no redirect took. Damage a redirect takes is not dealt to the player. If all of a column's combat damage to a player is redirected, the column has dealt that player no combat damage: Lethal kills no one, Thieving draws nothing, and nothing that triggers when a column deals combat damage to a player triggers. If some of it gets past the redirects (Piercing excess), the column has dealt the player that much. An ability that triggers when its column deals combat damage, with no player named (Vroot), does trigger on a redirected hit: the column dealt that damage to the unit that took it (see rule combat.damage.triggers.my-column).

text: Abilities that trigger during the combat damage step trigger during battle, so an effect that makes abilities cost more to trigger during battle applies to them.

examples.text: Crevice Lurker taxes a combat-damage trigger; on the same board without the Lurker there is no tax.

printed.quote: Abilities cost [one] more to activate or trigger during battle.

owner.quote: **[R121] is widened, and the widening is the printed text.** Crevice Lurker prints

text: An ability that works only while its card is in the bin can trigger on combat damage only if the card is already in the bin when that damage is dealt. A unit destroyed by combat damage is not in the bin while that same damage is dealt, but a unit destroyed in an earlier sub-step is.

examples.text: Cinder Scuttler is destroyed in the same sub-step in which another of its controller's columns deals combat damage to the opponent. It does not return.
examples.test: 310-zone-abilities.test.ts::§3 Cinder Scuttler does NOT recall off the damage step it died in

examples.text: A Swift unit destroys Cinder Scuttler in the Swift sub-step; in the normal sub-step its controller deals combat damage to the opponent, and it returns.
examples.test: 310-zone-abilities.test.ts::§4 but a Swift unit bins it BEFORE the normal step
